# Evaluation on 40 held-out synthetic people (set b: E41-E80)

**Synthetic data, not validated with real people.** Generated by `python scripts/eval.py --write` on 2026-11-17 at commit `641f749`. Every number below is computed by the script; none is typed by hand. Rules: [eval/LABELING.md](../eval/LABELING.md). People: [eval/personas.json](../eval/personas.json). Labels: [eval/labels.json](../eval/labels.json), sha256 `67fc77fe212a6e9b…`, written by an independent annotator that saw only the stories, before any of these people was run through the app.

Each share: value (count/people; 95% Wilson interval). With 40 people an interval is about ±15 points wide, so small differences between versions are not evidence of anything.

How the versions were run: the same 40 profiles through each version's own API. `641f749` ran from a temporary git worktree. v1 knew 25 IT roles only and could read only education, skill levels and tools (its interest questions and IT-area preferences have no counterpart in these profiles), so most of its gap is coverage, not a better algorithm. v1 has no idea of a person's status, so its "job-search courses for people in work" are counted by the same rule.

## Why first moves concentrate (found after the first run; nothing was changed because of it)

For each of the 31 people whose first move is not in their acceptable list, the first move is compared with the best-placed acceptable occupation in their top 50 (moderate adoption). Mean points the first move is ahead by, per part of the match score:

| Part (weight) | Mean lead | First move ahead in |
|---|---|---|
| field (20%) | -0.2 | 5 of 31 |
| interest (15%) | -0.4 | 13 of 31 |
| skill (30%) | -0.7 | 11 of 31 |
| outlook (35%) | +5.7 | 28 of 31 |

- Malaysian demand, which is most of the outlook, has 15 distinct values over 910 occupations; 111 occupations share the top value 90.6 (on the MyCOL list, in the MASCO major group whose share of job ads grew most).
- 190 occupations count as on the MyCOL list, through 60 MyCOL titles: an occupation inherits "yes" from the ISCO-08 unit group it maps to.
- 36 occupations map to ISCO major group 2 (professionals) while O*NET's job zone is 3 or less, for example: Tax Preparers → 2411 Accountants; Network and Computer Systems Administrators → 2523 Computer network professionals; Computer Systems Engineers/Architects → 2511 Systems analysts; Desktop Publishers → 2166 Graphic and multimedia designers. Such a mapping gives the professionals' job-ad signal. The raw ESCO crosswalk rows behind them have not been rechecked.
- Any fix (finer demand, MyCOL by exact title, a checked crosswalk) has to be tested on new synthetic people, not on these 40.

## Limits

- The people and their labels are synthetic. One annotator (an AI agent) wrote the labels; no second annotator checked them, so label noise is unmeasured.
- Agreement means "a counsellor would accept this", not "this person would succeed in it".
- Interest answers are made from each person's three liked types by one fixed rule (`scripts/eval_personas.py`), not answered by people.
- Phase 1 KPI 1 (career clarity of 20+ real testers) cannot be measured this way: see [impact_verification.md](impact_verification.md) and the pilot plan in the README.
